title: A pattern holding tens of thousands of selectors is compiled instead of refused
text_rewritten:
A caller can hand us a pattern that is a comma-separated list of tens of thousands of selectors. It compiles, and from then on every match against it costs proportionally, so one request degrades the whole service. No legitimate pattern is that large, so compiling one should fail fast with a ValueError instead of handing back a matcher.

The ceiling has to count every selector the pattern pulls in, not only the ones written at the top level. Selectors reached through a matches-any group such as :is(...) and selectors reached through a caller-supplied :--name alias must count as well, otherwise the same volume simply moves one level down and the ceiling buys nothing. Pick a fixed ceiling on the order of ten thousand selectors and document it. Ordinary patterns -- a few hundred selectors at most -- must keep compiling and selecting exactly as they do today.
body:
A caller can hand us a pattern that is a comma-separated list of tens of thousands of selectors. It compiles, and from then on every match against it costs proportionally, so one request degrades the whole service. No legitimate pattern is that large, so compiling one should fail fast with a ValueError instead of handing back a matcher.

The ceiling has to count every selector the pattern pulls in, not only the ones written at the top level. Selectors reached through a matches-any group such as :is(...) and selectors reached through a caller-supplied :--name alias must count as well, otherwise the same volume simply moves one level down and the ceiling buys nothing. Pick a fixed ceiling on the order of ten thousand selectors and document it. Ordinary patterns -- a few hundred selectors at most -- must keep compiling and selecting exactly as they do today.
acceptance_hint: Compiling a pattern whose total selector count is far above the documented ceiling raises ValueError, including when the bulk arrives through :is() or a custom :--name alias; a few hundred selectors still compile and select normally.
